status: G4 rest: processed, compressed and reviewed; ships as g4-camel-couched, in Chapter IX (the desktop app only)
use: A dromedary couched at rest beside the caravan baggage in a court beyond the board (Chapter IX).

generator.prompt: A dromedary camel of the Syrian desert caravans, mid-3rd century AD, couched at rest: lying on the ground with all four legs folded neatly beneath its body, the long neck curving up with the head raised level and facing forward, symmetrical. A single-humped camel with a sandy-tan coat, darker shaggy hair on the hump, neck and upper legs, a woven red and ochre saddle blanket over the hump held by a girth, and a plain rope halter. Realistic proportions, anatomically accurate. Single isolated model with complete geometry from every side and a bold, solid, readable silhouette from above. No ground plane, no display plinth, no text or inscriptions, no modern objects, no fantasy elements.

review.scope: Tripo's own render, four views of the final compressed model with a 1.8 m figure for scale (scripts/assets/preview-model.mjs), and the camps in the desktop build at High
review.notes: As asked: a sandy dromedary resting on its folded legs, its long neck curving up, under a patterned red and ochre blanket held by a girth. Two short wooden posts stand at the blanket's front and back, as a saddle's frame would, which the negative prompt named; they are small, and it was kept. It came facing nearly its +z and was turned 85 degrees to face +x: 2.50 m long and 1.6 m high. It stands only in the baggage line of Chapter IX's battles, which this review did not see in the game.
